name: Tree
unit: one mature tree, living for a year
headline: A single mature oak can support more than 2,300 other species. On a hot day, the shade and evaporation from one large tree cool like ten air conditioners.
why: Absorbs roughly 10–25 kg of CO₂ a year and stores it for as long as the wood lasts.
Roots hold soil, slow floods and let rain soak into the ground; leaves return water to the air and feed rainfall downwind.
Filters air pollution and cools streets. People with trees nearby have lower stress and heal faster.
A habitat in its own right: insects, birds, fungi, lichens, mammals.
Shade, beauty, fruit and a reason to be outside. Tree-lined streets are measurably more sociable.
stages: Growth|2|Carbon uptake speeds up with size
Old age & deadwood|3|Hollows and rot feed a fifth of woodland species
Fallen|2|Returns its nutrients to the soil
deps: Fungi in the soil|Trees trade sugar for water and minerals through an underground network.
Pollinators and seed carriers|Jays plant most of the oaks.
Time|The big, old trees do most of the work, and cannot be replaced in a human lifetime.
alts: Protect the old ones|One big tree stores more carbon and shelters more life than hundreds of saplings.|3,3.5,4,5,3.5|EASY|0|0
Plant a native tree in the right place|Local species support many times more wildlife than exotic ones. It will take decades to match an old tree.|3,3.5,4,5,3.5|MEDIUM|20|0
Water a street tree in a heatwave|Young city trees often die of thirst in their first summers.|3,3.5,4,5,4|EASY|0|0
qa: Can we plant our way out of climate change?|No. Trees help, but there is not enough land to absorb current emissions, and new trees take decades to matter. Cutting emissions and protecting existing forest come first.
Why do old trees matter so much?|A tree's carbon uptake keeps rising as it grows, and features like hollows, deadwood and deep bark only appear after a century or more.
Do trees really talk to each other?|They exchange carbon and chemical signals through shared fungal networks. How much this matters for forest health is still debated by scientists.
src: Bastin et al., Science 2019 and responses

name: Plant
unit: one potted plant or garden plant for a year
headline: Houseplants don't really clean indoor air: you would need hundreds in one room. What they measurably improve is your mood and attention.
why: The plant absorbs a trivial amount of CO₂. Heated greenhouses, transport and peat compost outweigh it.
A little watering. Garden lawns can be thirsty.
Caring for plants reduces stress and improves concentration.
A pot plant is neutral; a garden with native flowers feeds pollinators. Peat compost destroys bogs that store more carbon than forests.
Shared gardens build neighbourhoods; plants make places feel cared for.
deps: Peat bogs|They cover 3% of land and hold about twice the carbon of all the world's forests.
Pollinators|For anything that flowers outdoors.
alts: Peat-free compost|The single biggest choice a gardener makes.|0,-0.5,2,1.5,1.5|EASY|5|0
Native flowers instead of lawn|Even a square metre feeds bees and butterflies.|0.5,0.5,2,3.5,2|MEDIUM|5|3000
Swap cuttings with a neighbour|Free plants, no greenhouse, a conversation.|0,-0.5,2,1,2.5|EASY|2|0
qa: Are cut flowers bad?|It depends where and when. Roses flown from Kenya or grown in heated Dutch greenhouses in winter have a high footprint. Local, seasonal flowers are low.
What about my lawn?|A mown lawn is close to a wildlife desert. Mowing less often, or leaving a patch long, quickly brings back flowers and insects.
src: Cummings & Waring, Journal of Exposure Science 2020

name: Dog
unit: one medium-sized dog for a year
headline: A medium dog's meat-based diet gives it a carbon pawprint of around 770 kg a year. Dog owners also walk about 22 minutes more every day and live longer.
why: Almost entirely the meat in its food.
Water to grow that food.
Owners are more active, less lonely and have a lower risk of dying after a heart attack.
Off-lead dogs disturb ground-nesting birds; waste and flea treatments pollute streams.
Companionship, routine and a reason to talk to strangers.
m: ≈ 22 more minutes of walking a day
stages: Waste|1|Bags and what is in them
deps: The livestock industry|Pet food uses a real share of the world's meat.
You|
alts: Food made from by-products, insects or lower-carbon meats|Chicken or insect-based food can halve the pawprint.|-3,-3,4,-1.5,4.5|EASY|300|100000
Don't overfeed|About half of pet dogs are overweight.|-3.5,-3,4.5,-2,4.5|EASY|100|40000
Lead on near wildlife; avoid spot-on flea drops before swimming|Protects nesting birds and river insects.|-4,-3.5,4,-0.5,4.5|EASY|0|0
Adopt, don't shop|Millions of dogs are waiting in shelters.|-4,-3.5,4,-2,5|MEDIUM|0|0
qa: Is having a dog bad for the planet?|It has a real footprint, comparable to a small share of a car. It also has large, well-evidenced benefits for human health and happiness. The app's job is to show both.
Why are flea treatments an issue?|Common spot-on insecticides wash off into rivers at levels that kill aquatic insects. Ask a vet whether your dog needs year-round treatment.
src: Perkins et al., Science of the Total Environment 2021

name: Cat
unit: one pet cat for a year
headline: Pet and stray cats kill billions of birds a year in the United States alone, making them the largest human-linked cause of bird deaths there.
why: A meat-only diet: about 300 kg CO₂e a year.
Water to produce that food.
Stroking a cat lowers stress; owners report less loneliness.
Outdoor cats hunt birds, reptiles and small mammals whether or not they are hungry.
Companionship, especially for people living alone.
deps: Fish and meat supply chains|
Local wildlife|
alts: Keep it in at dawn and dusk|When birds are most vulnerable. Also safer for the cat.|-3.5,-3,3,-2,3.5|EASY|0|0
Bright collar or bell|Brightly coloured collar covers cut bird catches by about half.|-3.5,-3,3,-2.5,3.5|EASY|0|0
Plant-based litter|Wood, paper or corn instead of mined clay.|-3,-3,3,-3,3.5|EASY|20|0
Neuter and adopt|Prevents the stray population that does most of the hunting.|-3.5,-3,3,-2.5,4|MEDIUM|0|0
qa: Can cats eat a plant-based diet?|Cats need nutrients found naturally only in animal tissue. Carefully formulated vegan cat foods exist, but the evidence is limited; talk to a vet first.
src: Willson et al., Global Ecology and Conservation 2015

name: Bird
unit: one wild bird for a year
headline: North America has lost nearly 3 billion birds since 1970: more than one in four. They went quietly, mostly from common species.
why: Seed-spreading birds help forests regrow and store carbon.
No meaningful effect.
Birdsong is measurably good for mental wellbeing.
Birds control insects, spread seeds, pollinate and clean up carcasses.
The most watched wildlife on Earth; a first connection to nature for millions.
stages: Migration|3|Some cross whole oceans without stopping
deps: Insects|Almost all land birds feed insects to their young.
Stopover sites|A migrating bird needs every link in the chain of wetlands and woods.
Dark skies|Most songbirds migrate at night and are drawn off course by lights.
alts: Make windows visible|Dot stickers or screens: glass kills up to a billion birds a year in the US.|0.5,0,2,4.5,2.5|EASY|0|0
Native plants, no pesticides|Feed the insects that feed the birds.|0.5,0.5,2,5,2.5|MEDIUM|0|0
Lights out during migration|Especially in tall buildings in spring and autumn.|1,0,2,4.5,2.5|EASY|5|0
Count them|Citizen-science bird counts are how we know any of this.|0.5,0,2.5,4,3.5|EASY|0|0
qa: Why are birds declining?|Habitat loss and intensive farming first, then cats, window collisions and climate change. Where wetlands have been protected, waterbirds have recovered strongly: it is reversible.

name: Bee & pollinators
unit: one pollinating insect, and the colony or population it belongs to, for a year
headline: Three out of four of the world's food crops depend at least partly on animals like this one for pollination: coffee, cocoa, apples, almonds, tomatoes.
why: Pollination helps plants reproduce and keep storing carbon.
No direct effect.
Pollinated crops provide most of our vitamins A and C and many other nutrients.
Almost 90% of wild flowering plants depend on animal pollination.
Pollination is worth hundreds of billions of dollars a year to farming, for free.
stages: Adult|3|Each flower visit is a transaction
Overwintering|2|In stems, soil and leaf litter
deps: Flowers from spring to autumn|A gap of a few weeks can starve a colony.
Untidy corners|Most wild bees nest in bare soil, dead stems or old wood.
A world with fewer insecticides|Neonicotinoids harm bees at doses too small to kill them outright.
alts: Plant flowers that bloom in sequence|Window boxes count.|0.5,0,3,5,4|EASY|0|0
Leave a messy patch|Long grass, dead stems, a log pile.|0.5,0,3,5,4|EASY|0|0
No garden pesticides|Most garden pest problems solve themselves when predators return.|0.5,0.5,3.5,5,4|EASY|0|0
Buy from farms that keep hedgerows|Organic and nature-friendly farm labels.|0.5,0.5,3,5,4.5|MEDIUM|0|0
qa: Should I keep honeybees to help?|Probably not. Honeybees are farmed animals and are not endangered. In cities, too many hives can outcompete the wild bees that are in trouble. Planting flowers helps all of them.

Are insects really disappearing?|Many long-term studies show steep declines, especially in farmland and for flying insects, though the picture varies by place and group. The causes are habitat loss, pesticides, light and climate.
src: Klein et al., Proceedings of the Royal Society B 2007

name: A human
unit: an average human lifestyle for one year. This is the world average, not a judgement of the person in view
headline: The only thing your camera will ever find that can change its own score. The richest 10% of people cause about half of all emissions; the poorest half, about a tenth.
why: The world average is about 4.7 tonnes of CO₂ a person each year. It ranges from under 0.1 tonnes to over 30 depending on where and how you live.
An average person's food, goods and energy use about 3,800 litres of water every day, almost all of it hidden in what we eat and buy.
Not scored. This one is up to you.
Humans and our livestock now make up 96% of the weight of all mammals on Earth. Wild mammals are the remaining 4%.
Not scored. Every act of care, teaching, building and kindness goes here. This one is up to you too.
m: 96% of mammal biomass is us and our livestock
stages: Food|3|About a quarter of a typical footprint
Voice & vote|3|The lever with no upper limit
deps: Everything else this app can see|Air from plankton and trees, food from soil and pollinators, water from rivers and aquifers.
Other people|
alts: Eat mostly plants|The biggest food lever.|-4.5,-4.5,2,-3,0|MEDIUM|800|400000
Go car-free or car-light|Often the biggest single personal lever in rich countries.|-4.5,-5,3,-3.5,1|BIG|2000|0
One fewer long flight a year|A tonne or more each time.|-4.5,-5,0,-4,0|MEDIUM|1500|0
Green your home energy|Heat pump, insulation, renewable tariff.|-4.5,-5,1,-4,0|BIG|1500|0
Use your voice|At work, in your town, with your vote and your savings. Systems change faster than habits.|-4,-4.5,1,-3,3|MEDIUM|0|0
qa: Is individual action pointless next to corporations and governments?|It is a false choice. Companies emit to make what people buy, and governments move when voters do. The most effective individuals change their own big-ticket habits and push the systems around them.

What are the choices that matter most?|In order, for most people in rich countries: how you travel, what you eat, how your home is heated, and where your money is invested. Recycling and light bulbs are good habits but small by comparison.

Is the planet overpopulated?|Impact depends far more on consumption than on headcount. A few hundred million high consumers account for most emissions; birth rates are already below replacement level in most of the world.
src: Oxfam / Stockholm Environment Institute, Climate Equality 2023

name: Cow & farm animals
unit: one beef or dairy cow for a year
headline: A cow burps about 100 kg of methane a year, warming the planet as much as driving a car some 12,000 km.
why: Around 2–3 tonnes of CO₂e a year from methane alone.
Feed and drinking water: a dairy cow drinks up to 100 litres a day.
Not scored for the animal itself; see beef and dairy.
Livestock and their feed use about 77% of farmland while providing 18% of our calories. Grazing at low density can maintain wildflower meadows.
Livestock support the livelihoods of over a billion people, many of them poor.
deps: Grass and feed crops|
Gut microbes|They do the digesting, and make the methane.
alts: Eat less, choose better|Lower demand is the main lever; pasture-raised and local where you do buy.|-3,-3,0,-2,1|MEDIUM|300|100000
Support nature-friendly farms|Low-density grazing can restore meadows and hedgerows.|-4.5,-4,0,-1,2|MEDIUM|0|0
qa: Can feed additives fix the methane?|Partly. Seaweed and synthetic additives can cut a cow's methane by 30% or more in trials, mainly for animals fed in barns. They do not change the land and water use.
src: FAO, Tackling Climate Change Through Livestock
Poore & Nemecek 2018 via Our World in Data

name: Building
unit: one home, lived in for a year
headline: Buildings cause over a third of the world's energy-related CO₂. Cement alone, if it were a country, would be the third-largest emitter on Earth.
why: Heating, cooling and electricity: several tonnes a year for a typical home in a cold or hot climate, plus the carbon locked into its concrete and steel.
Around 140 litres per person every day indoors.
Shelter is a foundation of health. Damp, cold or overheated homes cause illness.
Building over land removes habitat; glass kills birds. Roofs, walls and gardens can host a surprising amount of life.
A secure home is the base for everything else in a life.
stages: Cement, steel, glass|3|Emitted before anyone moves in
Demolition|2|Construction waste is the largest waste stream
deps: The energy grid and gas network|
Sand|The most-mined material on Earth; concrete-grade sand is running short in places.
alts: Insulate and draught-proof|The energy you never need is the cleanest.|-4,-4,4,-2.5,4|MEDIUM|600|0
Turn heating down 1 °C|Saves around 10% of heating energy.|-4.5,-4,3.5,-2.5,4|EASY|300|0
Heat pump when the boiler dies|Three to four times more efficient than burning gas.|-3.5,-4,4,-2.5,4|BIG|1500|0
Renovate rather than rebuild|The greenest building is usually the one that already exists.|-4,-4,3.5,-1.5,4|BIG|0|0
Give the outside to wildlife|Swift boxes, green roofs, bird-safe glass.|-5,-4,3.5,-1,4.5|MEDIUM|0|0
qa: What is embodied carbon?|The emissions from making the materials and constructing the building. For a new, efficient building it can equal decades of running it, which is why reusing buildings matters.
Why is cement so carbon-heavy?|Making it means heating limestone to about 1,450 °C, and the chemical reaction itself releases CO₂. Roughly 8% of global emissions come from cement.
src: UNEP Global Status Report for Buildings and Construction 2022

name: Solar panel
unit: one rooftop solar panel, generating for a year
headline: This panel repays all the carbon used to make it in one to three years, then generates clean power for another twenty-five. Solar is now the cheapest electricity in history.
why: Generates around 400–600 kWh a year, avoiding about 250 kg of CO₂ on an average grid. Scored as a replacement for grid power.
Uses almost no water, unlike coal, gas and nuclear plants, which need it for cooling.
Every unit of coal power it displaces means less of the air pollution that kills millions a year.
Rooftops use no extra land. Large solar farms can be good or bad for wildlife depending on how they are managed.
Cheap, local energy and many jobs. But a large share of the world's polysilicon comes from Xinjiang, where forced labour has been documented.
stages: Recycling|1|About 95% of materials are recoverable; capacity is still being built
deps: Sunlight|
Silicon, silver, aluminium, glass|
A grid or battery|To use the power when the sun is not shining.
alts: Use power when the sun shines|Run the washing machine and charge the car at midday.|4.5,1,3,1,1|EASY|100|0
Ask where the panels were made|Traceable supply chains exist and demand moves the market.|4,1,3,1,2.5|MEDIUM|0|0
No roof? Join a community solar scheme or switch tariff|You do not need to own the panel.|4,1,3,1,2|EASY|400|0
qa: Does making panels emit more than they save?|No. The energy and carbon payback is one to three years in most places, against a working life of twenty-five to thirty.
What happens to old panels?|Most have not yet reached end of life. They are largely glass and aluminium and can be recycled; the industry is scaling up to do so.
src: Sheffield Hallam University, In Broad Daylight 2021

name: Wild nature
unit: this piece of the living world, for a year
headline: The ocean has absorbed about a quarter of all the CO₂ we have emitted and more than 90% of the extra heat. Everything else this app scans depends on places like this.
why: Oceans, forests, wetlands and soils absorb about half of human CO₂ emissions every year.
Wetlands, forests and mountains store, filter and release almost all the freshwater we use.
Two hours a week in nature is linked to markedly better health and wellbeing.
This is biodiversity. Wildlife populations monitored since 1970 have fallen by an average of 73%.
Sacred, shared and free. Over a billion people depend directly on forests and reefs for food and income.
stages: Plants & plankton|3|Make the oxygen and the food
deps: A stable climate|
Being left enough room|Scientists and governments have agreed a goal of protecting 30% of land and sea by 2030.
Us|It now depends on human choices.
alts: Go more often|People protect what they know.|4,5,5,5,4.5|EASY|0|0
Leave no trace, take a bag|Pick up three pieces of litter each visit.|4,5,4.5,5,4.5|EASY|0|0
Join or fund a local conservation group|Small local groups protect a remarkable amount of land.|4.5,5,4.5,5,5|MEDIUM|0|0
Record what you see|Wildlife recording apps turn a walk into data scientists use.|4,5,4.5,5,4.5|EASY|0|0
qa: Is it too late?|No. Where pressure is removed, nature recovers faster than expected: whales, wolves, beavers, seagrass and forests have all rebounded when given space and time.

What does a 73% decline mean?|It is the average change in size of monitored wildlife populations, not the share of animals lost. It still signals a severe, widespread decline, steepest in rivers and lakes.

name: Clothing or accessory
unit: one item of clothing or an accessory over its life
headline: The world now buys about 60% more clothes than it did 15 years ago, and keeps each one for half as long.
why: Fashion causes somewhere between 2% and 8% of global emissions, depending on what is counted.
Growing fibres and dyeing fabric are both water-intensive.
Safe to wear; risks fall on farm and factory workers.
Pesticides on cotton, microplastics from synthetics, and huge volumes of waste.
Tens of millions of garment workers earn less than a living wage.
stages: End of life|2|A truckload of textiles is landfilled or burned every second
deps: Low-wage labour|
Cheap energy and water|
alts: Wear what you own, more|The 30-wears test: will you wear it at least 30 times?|-2,-2,-0.5,-1.5,-1.5|EASY|20|5000
Second-hand first|Skips nearly all of the making.|-0.5,-0.5,0,0,0.5|EASY|40|10000
Repair and care|Wash cold, mend small damage.|-2,-2,-0.5,-1.5,-1.5|EASY|20|2000
qa: What's the most sustainable fabric?|There isn't one. The most sustainable garment is the one already in your wardrobe, worn many times.
src: Ellen MacArthur Foundation, A New Textiles Economy

name: Household object
unit: one manufactured object over its life
headline: Humanity now uses over 100 billion tonnes of materials a year. Only about 7% of that is cycled back into use.
why: Extracting and processing materials causes about half of global emissions.
Mining and manufacturing use and pollute water.
Most objects are harmless in use; the risks are upstream.
Material extraction causes over 90% of land-related biodiversity loss and water stress.
Manufacturing employs hundreds of millions, with conditions that vary widely.
deps: Mines and forests somewhere else|
A long supply chain you cannot see|
